cues.en: Mike Cohen: In this video, I'm going to introduce you to entropy and how to compute entropy.
cues.zh: Mike Cohen：這部影片會介紹熵，以及如何計算熵。

cues.en: And in particular, I'm gonna talk about Shannon entropy.
cues.zh: 具體來說，我要談的是夏農熵。

cues.en: And I make that distinction clear because there are actually several different kinds of entropy.
cues.zh: 特別強調這個區別，是因為熵其實有好幾種。

cues.en: There's several different interpretations of the term entropy in different fields, and that's actually where I'm gonna start this lecture.
cues.zh: 不同領域對熵這個詞有不同的解釋，我就從這裡開始講起。

cues.en: So when you think about the concept of entropy, if you've come across this term before, what you might initially think about is the concept of entropy from physics.
cues.zh: 如果你以前接觸過熵這個詞，想到熵的概念時，最先想到的可能是物理學中的熵。

cues.en: And this is the idea that systems that are in a state of order, so an organized system, will naturally over time lead to a system
cues.zh: 它的概念是，處於有序狀態的系統，也就是有組織的系統，會隨時間自然轉變成

cues.en: that is less organized.
cues.zh: 組織程度較低的系統。

cues.en: So basically things decay, things become more chaotic over time.
cues.zh: 基本上就是事物會衰敗，隨時間變得更混亂。

cues.en: That is the physics concept of entropy.
cues.zh: 這就是物理學中熵的概念。

cues.en: And essentially it means that we're all gonna die and the universe will decay into an empty pit of nothingness.
cues.zh: 基本上，它意味著我們都會死，而宇宙也會衰敗成空無一物的深淵。

cues.en: Rather dismal, but unfortunately that is the truth.
cues.zh: 相當悲觀，但不幸的是，這就是事實。

cues.en: We might as well live with it and continue to enjoy our lives.
cues.zh: 我們不如接受它，繼續享受人生。

cues.en: Anyway, this is not the kind of entropy that I'm referring to here in this video.
cues.zh: 總之，這不是我在這部影片中所指的熵。

cues.en: Instead, I'm referring to entropy in the information processing interpretation.
cues.zh: 這裡指的是資訊處理詮釋下的熵。

cues.en: And that comes from this guy, Claude Shannon.
cues.zh: 這個概念來自這位 Claude Shannon。

cues.en: And he made, he was a mathematician and a scientist, and he developed a theory of information and information transmission.
cues.zh: 他是一位數學家和科學家，建立了資訊與資訊傳輸的理論。

cues.en: It's been hugely important.
cues.zh: 這個理論極為重要。

cues.en: And in fact a lot of the current protocols that we have that the internet relies on, like TCP IP and HTTP, FTP, a lot of these information transmission
cues.zh: 事實上，網際網路目前依賴的許多通訊協定，例如 TCP/IP、HTTP、FTP，很多這類資訊傳輸

cues.en: protocols can basically all be linked back to the original theoretical work by Claude Shannon.
cues.zh: 協定，基本上都可以追溯到 Claude Shannon 最初的理論工作。

cues.en: So this form of entropy is related to how much surprise or information there exists in a system.
cues.zh: 所以這種熵，和系統中有多少意外性或資訊有關。

cues.en: So entropy and information theory is a little bit brighter.
cues.zh: 因此，資訊理論中的熵比較光明一些。

cues.en: It says that everything is great and happy and surprising things convey more information.
cues.zh: 它說一切都很美好、很快樂，而令人意外的事情會傳遞更多資訊。

cues.en: Okay, well this first part is not really, well, it is true.
cues.zh: 好，前面那一部分其實不完全是……嗯，也是真的。

cues.en: Everything is well, many things are great and we should be happy.
cues.zh: 一切都……很多事情都很美好，我們應該快樂。

cues.en: But what information or Shannon information really does say, entropy, is that surprising things convey more information.
cues.zh: 但資訊，或者說夏農資訊、熵，真正要表達的是：令人意外的事情會傳遞更多資訊。

cues.en: So here you see a graph of entropy as a function of the probability of a certain event happening, and this is the probability of a binary event.
cues.zh: 這張圖顯示熵如何隨某個事件發生的機率而變化，這裡是二元事件的機率。

cues.en: So you can imagine that this would be the probability similar to a binomial distribution that I introduced you to a while back.
cues.zh: 你可以把它想成類似我之前介紹的二項分布中的機率。

cues.en: Let's imagine this is a probability of a sports team winning a particular game.
cues.zh: 假設這代表某支球隊贏得一場比賽的機率。

cues.en: So a sports team can either win or lose.
cues.zh: 球隊不是贏，就是輸。

cues.en: That's a binary outcome.
cues.zh: 這是二元結果。

cues.en: And the idea of Shannon entropy, information entropy, is that when we know for sure that something either will happen or won't happen,
cues.zh: 夏農熵，也就是資訊熵的概念是：如果我們確定某件事必然發生，或必然不會發生，

cues.en: then that has very little information.
cues.zh: 它所包含的資訊就很少。

cues.en: There's very little surprise, very little information.
cues.zh: 幾乎沒有意外性，也幾乎沒有資訊。

cues.en: But as the probability approaches, whatever is the probability value of least certainty, and that would be 0.5 for a binary outcome.
cues.zh: 但當機率接近最不確定的機率值，而二元結果的這個值就是 0.5，

cues.en: As we approach a value, probability value with more and more uncertainty, then the entropy increases.
cues.zh: 當機率值越來越不確定時，熵就會增加。

cues.en: So that's the concept.
cues.zh: 這就是這個概念。

cues.en: Basically the more surprising something is, the less certain something is, then the more information it conveys, and therefore the more entropy that system has.
cues.zh: 基本上，一件事越令人意外、越不確定，就會傳遞越多資訊，因此系統具有的熵也越高。

cues.en: Okay, so here is the formula to compute entropy.
cues.zh: 好，這就是計算熵的公式。

cues.en: It's actually a pretty simple formula, despite the fact that there's a lot of letters in this line here.
cues.zh: 雖然這一行有很多字母，但公式其實很簡單。

cues.en: So what we do is we compute the probability of a certain data value or a certain event taking place, and then we multiply that probability
cues.zh: 先計算某個資料值出現，或某個事件發生的機率，再把這個機率

cues.en: by the log of that probability.
cues.zh: 乘以該機率的對數。

cues.en: So you can see that the probability appears here twice, once outside the logarithm and once inside the logarithm.
cues.zh: 所以你可以看到，機率在這裡出現兩次，一次在對數外面，一次在對數裡面。

cues.en: Now notice here that what we are actually multiplying are the probabilities of the data values, not the data values themselves.
cues.zh: 注意，實際相乘的是資料值的機率，而不是資料值本身。

cues.en: So before computing entropy, you first need to convert your data values into probabilities, okay?
cues.zh: 因此，在計算熵之前，必須先把資料值轉換成機率，好嗎？

cues.en: So then you have to sum up over all of the probabilities for all the different events.
cues.zh: 接著，將所有不同事件的機率所對應的項加總。

cues.en: And then we attach a minus sign here and that gives us our measure of entropy of that system.
cues.zh: 然後在這裡加上負號，就得到該系統的熵量值。

cues.en: Now, the reason why we have a negative sign is just for convenience.
cues.zh: 使用負號只是為了方便。

cues.en: When you take the logarithm of a number that's less than one, so log can't be, or you can't take the log of a negative number, but the logarithm of a number between zero
cues.zh: 當你對小於 1 的數取對數時……對數不能，或者說，你不能對負數取對數；但介於 0

cues.en: and one is going to give you a negative number.
cues.zh: 與 1 之間的數，其對數會是負數。

cues.en: So therefore all of this stuff ends up being a negative number and that, you know, it isn't such a big deal.
cues.zh: 所以這一整項最後會得到負數，其實也沒什麼大不了。

cues.en: It would basically flip this entropy curve here.
cues.zh: 基本上只是把這條熵曲線翻過來。

cues.en: So it would look like an upright U like this from zero down to minus one.
cues.zh: 看起來就會是這種開口向上的 U 形，從 0 往下到 −1。

cues.en: So it's, you know, nicer to think about increasing entropy as a positive number.
cues.zh: 所以，把熵的增加想成正數，會比較直觀。

cues.en: So that's why we have the minus sign in here.
cues.zh: 這就是這裡加上負號的原因。

cues.en: Alright, so that's the formula.
cues.zh: 好，這就是公式。

cues.en: What types of data can this formula be applied to?
cues.zh: 這個公式可以用在哪些資料類型上呢？

cues.en: I would like you to take a moment and think about the different kinds of data, different data types, and whether each data type is appropriate for this formula.
cues.zh: 請你花一點時間想想各種資料、不同的資料類型，以及每種資料類型是否適用這個公式。

cues.en: So the answer is that this formula can be applied to nominal data, ordinal data, so basically categorical data and also discreet numerical data.
cues.zh: 答案是，這個公式可以用於名目資料、次序資料，也就是類別資料，以及離散數值資料。

cues.en: Now, if you have interval or ratio data, you cannot really apply this because what is the probability of a, of you know,
cues.zh: 如果你有區間資料或比率資料，就不能直接這樣使用，因為某個

cues.en: exactly some very precise height existing in the population?
cues.zh: 極為精確的特定身高，在母體中出現的機率是多少呢？

cues.en: That probability is essentially zero for interval or ratio data.
cues.zh: 對區間資料或比率資料而言，這個機率基本上是 0。

cues.en: So if you have interval or ratio data, what do you think we should do about that?
cues.zh: 因此，如果資料是區間資料或比率資料，你認為該怎麼做呢？

cues.en: Well, I assume you guessed the right answer.
cues.zh: 我想你應該猜到正確答案了。

cues.en: We can convert it to discreet numeric data by binning.
cues.zh: 可以透過分箱，將它轉換成離散數值資料。

cues.en: And this is done essentially by creating a histogram.
cues.zh: 這基本上就是建立直方圖。

cues.en: Alright, but when you do this, you have to be mindful that the entropy you will measure depends on the bin size and the bin number or the bin number.
cues.zh: 但這麼做時必須留意，測得的熵會取決於區間大小和區間數，或者說區間數。

cues.en: So the way that you discretize interval or ratio data will actually affect the measure of entropy or the estimate of entropy that you get for that dataset.
cues.zh: 因此，將區間資料或比率資料離散化的方式，實際上會影響你對這組資料測得或估計出的熵。

cues.en: You'll get to discover this for yourself in a few videos from now in code.
cues.zh: 再過幾部影片，你就會透過程式親自探索這件事。

cues.en: Okay, so how do we interpret entropy?
cues.zh: 好，我們該如何解讀熵？

cues.en: Well, entropy of a signal or a dataset is essentially telling us about the variability in that dataset.
cues.zh: 訊號或資料集的熵，基本上是在告訴我們這組資料的變異程度。

cues.en: So high entropy means that the dataset has a lot of variability.
cues.zh: 高熵表示資料集具有很大的變異。

cues.en: It means that the data take on a lot of different kinds of values.
cues.zh: 代表資料會取很多不同的值。

cues.en: And conversely, low entropy of a dataset means that most of the values of the dataset are very similar to each other.
cues.zh: 相反地，資料集的熵低，表示其中大部分數值都很相似。

cues.en: They repeat and therefore they're redundant.
cues.zh: 它們會重複，因此具有冗餘性。

cues.en: So there's a lot less information in the total dataset when the entropy is low.
cues.zh: 所以熵低時，整組資料所包含的資訊就少得多。

cues.en: Now this might sound familiar, it might sound a little bit like the concept of variance, and in fact, in some sense, entropy and variants are measuring kind of similar features
cues.zh: 這聽起來可能很熟悉，有點像變異數的概念。事實上，在某種意義下，熵與變異數衡量的是資料中

cues.en: of the data.
cues.zh: 有些相似的特性。

cues.en: The key, one key difference is that entropy is a non-linear measure.
cues.zh: 一個關鍵差異是，熵是非線性的量值。

cues.en: It also makes zero assumptions about the shape of the distribution.
cues.zh: 它也完全不假設分布的形狀。

cues.en: We don't have to care about what the distribution looks like.
cues.zh: 我們不必在意分布長什麼樣子。

cues.en: In contrast, variance depends on the validity and the appropriateness of the mean, and therefore, variance is really only appropriate
cues.zh: 相較之下，變異數依賴平均值是否有效、是否適用，因此變異數其實只適合

cues.en: for roughly normally distributed data.
cues.zh: 大致呈常態分布的資料。

cues.en: So data that have some kind of a peak towards the center, and they decay towards the edges.
cues.zh: 也就是中央附近有某種峰值，而且向兩側逐漸下降的資料。

cues.en: So with entropy, you don't have that constraint.
cues.zh: 使用熵就沒有這個限制。

cues.en: Entropy is used in some machine learning techniques and some deep learning techniques.
cues.zh: 熵用於一些機器學習技術，以及一些深度學習技術。

cues.en: It's used for optimization.
cues.zh: 它可以用於最佳化。

cues.en: It's used to look at coherence or coupling between different systems.
cues.zh: 也可以用來研究不同系統之間的相干性或耦合。

cues.en: That would be a quantity called mutual information.
cues.zh: 那會是一個稱為互資訊的量。

cues.en: I'm not gonna talk a whole lot about entropy in this course, but I do think it's important for you to understand the concept and the formula
cues.zh: 這門課不會花很多時間談熵，但我認為你應該理解這個概念、公式，

cues.en: and the basic interpretation of Shannon entropy.
cues.zh: 以及夏農熵的基本解讀方式。

cues.en: In terms of the units of entropy, when you write out or when you compute entropy using log base two, that's the common convention.
cues.zh: 至於熵的單位，當你寫出或計算熵時，通常會使用以 2 為底的對數。

cues.en: That's what's most often done.
cues.zh: 這是最常見的做法。

cues.en: That gives you units in terms of bits.
cues.zh: 得到的單位是位元，也就是 bit。

cues.en: So one value of entropy, an entropy of one means one bit of entropy.
cues.zh: 所以熵值為 1，就代表有 1 bit 的熵。

cues.en: And the reason why it's called a bit is because bit is for binary.
cues.zh: 之所以稱為 bit，是因為 bit 代表二進位。

cues.en: You think of a computer bit as being true or false or on or off.
cues.zh: 你可以把電腦的一個位元想成真或假、開或關。

cues.en: So the maximum entropy that a binary process can have is one.
cues.zh: 因此，二元過程所能具有的最大熵是 1。

cues.en: So one bit, but this is not the only possibility.
cues.zh: 也就是 1 bit，但這不是唯一的選擇。

cues.en: There's other bases for log.
cues.zh: 對數還可以使用其他底數。

cues.en: So there's also the natural log.
cues.zh: 例如自然對數。

cues.en: Notice these two equations are exactly the same.
cues.zh: 注意，這兩個方程式完全相同。

cues.en: We're just using the log base two here is log base E.
cues.zh: 只是一個使用以 2 為底的對數，這裡則是以 e 為底。

cues.en: So then you call it nats.
cues.zh: 這時就稱為 nat。

cues.en: Now if you're comparing entropy across different data sets or different individuals, different experiments, it doesn't actually matter as long as the units are consistent,
cues.zh: 如果要比較不同資料集、不同個體、不同實驗的熵，只要單位一致，實際上使用哪個都無所謂，

cues.en: then you can compare entropy across different data sets.
cues.zh: 就可以比較不同資料集的熵。

cues.en: This really just affects the units, whether it's in bits or nats.
cues.zh: 這實際上只會影響單位是 bit 還是 nat。

cues.en: Before closing, there's one thing that I want to mention, which I forgot to say before, and that is that when we say surprise here, surprise in the context of information theory
cues.zh: 結束前，我想提一件剛才忘了說的事。這裡所謂的意外性，在資訊理論的情境中，

cues.en: is not exactly the same as the way you would probably use surprise in your day-to-day life.
cues.zh: 和你日常生活中使用「意外」這個詞的方式，不完全相同。

cues.en: So for example, let's say, you know there's a, someone throws you a surprise birthday party.
cues.zh: 例如，假設有人為你辦了一場驚喜生日派對。

cues.en: So the probability of getting a surprise birthday party, you would consider that probability to be very small, but then you actually get a surprise birthday party.
cues.zh: 你可能認為遇上驚喜生日派對的機率很低，但結果真的有人為你辦了驚喜生日派對。

cues.en: So you're really surprised.
cues.zh: 所以你非常驚訝。

cues.en: So you might think that surprise should mean something where the probability is very low and it happens, or when the probability is very high and it doesn't happen.
cues.zh: 你可能會認為，意外代表機率很低的事發生了，或機率很高的事卻沒發生。

cues.en: That's kind of our colloquial interpretation of the word surprise.
cues.zh: 這是我們日常語言中對「意外」的理解。

cues.en: But in information theory, surprise actually means things that are unpredictable.
cues.zh: 但在資訊理論中，意外性實際上指的是無法預測的事物。

cues.en: So the less you can predict the outcome of an experiment or a signal, then the more surprise that phenomenon has.
cues.zh: 越無法預測實驗或訊號的結果，這個現象就具有越多意外性。

cues.en: So you can think of it with a coin toss.
cues.zh: 你可以用擲硬幣來理解。

cues.en: You cannot predict, assuming it's a fair coin, you cannot predict what the outcome of a coin toss is going to be.
cues.zh: 假設硬幣是公平的，你就無法預測擲硬幣的結果。

cues.en: So therefore it has a lot of surprise.
cues.zh: 因此，它具有很高的意外性。
